title: Forest fire incidents fall this dry season, one major fire in Wangdue
detail: The Department of Forests and Park Services said fire cases and burnt area fell compared with the previous dry season; most were controlled quickly except one major fire in Wangdue Phodrang.
attribution: Department of Forests and Park Services via BBS

title: Changzamtog fire in Thimphu displaces 11 families
detail: Kuensel reported a fire in Changzamtog on 26 April displaced 11 families and raised concerns about unregulated temporary structures and building-safety enforcement.

title: Flood-damaged Dagachhu hydropower plant to restart 16 May
detail: The Department of Energy said restoration of the flood-damaged Dagachhu hydropower plant was nearly complete, with machinery start-up scheduled for 16 May 2026.

title: Climate-resilient bridge completed in flood-hit Dechencholing
detail: BBS reported a Nu 25 million, flood-resilient bridge was completed in Dechencholing, Thimphu, replacing hume pipes that blocked and overflowed; the area was devastated by an August 2024 flash flood.

title: Global roadshow for USD 190M Gelephu–Tareythang road and bridges project
detail: Kuensel reported an international roadshow began to attract contractors for the USD 190 million Gelephu–Tareythang road and bridges project, part of Gelephu Mindfulness City, including a 1,005 m bridge with elephant crossings.

title: M5.5 earthquake near Punakha damages 404 households
detail: BBS, citing the Department of Local Governance and Disaster Management, reported a 23:36 quake centred in Punakha (~20 km deep) damaged 404 households mainly in Wangdue Phodrang, Punakha and Monggar, plus schools and monuments; one person injured in Lhuentse, no deaths.
attribution: Department of Local Governance and Disaster Management via BBS

title: Recurring landslide debris floods Phuentsholing–Samtse highway at Amochhu
detail: BBS reported an active upstream landslide has washed debris onto the highway near the fuel depot almost nightly since mid-May, blocking traffic for hours; Phuentsholing Thromde said the problem exceeds its capacity and halted night clearance for worker safety.

title: Amochhu flooding disrupts exports and labour-permit processing
detail: BBS reported recurring Amochhu floods and road blockages delayed boulder exports and foreign-worker permits (2–3 days); Thromde said it had spent over Nu 2 million on clearance by 8 June and floodwater had entered the NHDCL housing colony.
attribution: Phuentsholing Thromde and labour agents via BBS

title: NCHM warns of extremely heavy rain over southern Bhutan
detail: NCHM issued a warning of heavy to very heavy rainfall over southern and isolated central areas valid 28–29 June 2026, following a 19 June advisory on very heavy rain in the south.
attribution: National Center for Hydrology and Meteorology warning

title: Overnight flooding in Phuentsholing displaces over 70 families
detail: Heavy rain on the night of 28–29 June flooded Chamkuna/Amochhu areas; BBS said over 70 families were displaced, 30+ evacuated from the Amochhu temporary settlement, a canteen destroyed and about 70% of ~1,300 LPG cylinders at Pemaling swept away; no casualties.

title: Flash flood washes away Bailey bridge, cutting off 75 households in Tsamang
detail: Evening flash flood in Ganglapong (Monggar) destroyed the only road bridge linking Tsamang gewog villages to Autsho; NCHM attributed it to heavy rain that may have partially breached the 2003 Tsatichhu landslide dam. No casualties.

title: OAG: SP+ capsules dominate drug trafficking cases in FY2025-26
detail: The Office of the Attorney General's annual report, as reported by BBS, said it handled 279 narcotics/psychotropic cases, 220 of them involving Spasmo Proxyvon Plus capsules; 31 involved brown sugar/heroin and 28 N10 tablets.
attribution: Office of the Attorney General annual report via BBS

title: Heritage Changyul Galem House collapses in Punakha
detail: The government acknowledged a conservation-funding gap after the nationally significant Changyul Galem House partially collapsed on 9 August; emergency stabilisation began 11 August. No casualties reported.
agency: Department of Culture and Dzongkha Development

title: PM: GLOF monitoring ongoing; Thorthormi siphoning pilot launched in Lunana
detail: PM Tshering Tobgay said Thorthormi and Rapstreng lakes pose the greatest threat; The Bhutanese reported 77 communities (1,196 households, 11,921 people) at risk across Gasa, Punakha, Wangdue and Tsirang, a siphoning pilot launched 9 Sept in Lunana and USD 22 million GCF support approved.
attribution: Prime Minister and NCHM figures via The Bhutanese

title: NCHM: fluctuating September rain and temperature swings amid El Niño
detail: NCHM forecast above-normal rain in early and late September with a drier, hotter mid-month in the south, and said a strong El Niño may persist to February 2027, with possible impacts on agriculture and hydropower.

title: GLOF preparedness in Samdingkha, Punakha; residents remain anxious
detail: BBS reported ~75 residents in 40 houses/shops at Samdingkha lie in the Phochhu GLOF path; 17 siren stations and 7 automatic water-level stations are installed along the Phochhu.

title: Thimphu police log 37 OTP/online-banking scam cases in two weeks
detail: The Bhutanese reported scammers used fake bank Facebook pages and a counterfeit app to capture logins and OTPs; Thimphu police received 37 cases in two weeks and froze accounts in most cases; one victim lost Nu 424,000, later largely recovered.
attribution: Royal Bhutan Police (Thimphu) via The Bhutanese

title: Air-quality concerns over Norbugang industrial park emissions
detail: The Bhutanese reported residents' concerns over smoke from Norbugang industrial park (Samtse); the Samtse Dzongda said heavy emissions are irregular and linked to machine breakdowns. DECC did not comment.

title: Traders allege goods from low-tax Sarpang smuggled to other districts
detail: The Traders Association of Bhutan told the Department of Revenue and Customs that goods imported under Sarpang's BST regime are moved illegally (allegedly hidden under sand/gravel loads) via Trongsa and Bumthang; DRC said it would investigate.
attribution: Traders Association allegation; DRC response via The Bhutanese

title: Extortion 'gunda tax' by Jaigaon network halts Bhutanese scrap exports
detail: The Bhutanese reported a network in Jaigaon (India) demanded Nu 10,000 per truck from Bhutanese scrap exporters, stalling exports through Phuentsholing; it said Jaigaon police later arrested five people.
attribution: Exporters and The Bhutanese reporting; arrests by Indian police
